newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Short Australian debt sparkling again.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Short Australian debt sparkling again.

text.p: FUTURES *SUP-RES *2ND SUP-RES *3RD SUP-RES *RSI
*Short Australian bond and bills futures raced higher in
after hours trading on the slight chance that Tuesday's RBA
board meeting endorsed a further easing in monetary policy.
*First quarter GDP due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT)
Short Australian bond and bills futures raced higher in after-hours trading on the slight chance that Tuesday's Reserve Bank board meeting endorsed a further easing in monetary policy.
Although such a move is generally seen as unlikeley, the market was not taking any risks given the out-of-the-blue cut in official rates to 5.5 percent on May 23.

June bill futures ended SYCOM at 94.65, up from Tuesday's 94.58 pit close and equating to a cash rate of 5.35 percent, while September was also up seven basis points at 94.69, and a near 20 basis point discount to cash.
The June three-year bond contract also firmed to 93.86 from a previous dayside close of 93.79, overcoming last week's 3-1/4 year peak of 93.83 which followed weak April retail trade data.
Initial resistance is pegged at 93.88 before the market seriously considers an advance of 94.00, analysts said.

"Follow through beyond 93.80 essentially demands the bills strip to do the leading. While bills prices seek to move onto their 94.75 price target levels, the best advice is to go with it," said Peter Pontikis, technical strategist at Westpac.
June 10-year bonds slightly lagged the advance, ending SYCOM at 92.700, up from Tuesday's pit close of 92.655.
This was still the contract's highest level since February, but the market now find itself in the thick of a 92.670/92.750 resistance bank, analysts said.
A further advance in U.S. Treasuries supported the local firm tone, and where hopes of considerably slower second quarter growth continues to underpin the rally.

Locally the market sees the first quarter GDP at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT). Forecasts centre on a 0.8 percent rise after the 0.5 percent increase in the December quarter. This would see the annual rate at 2.2 percent from 3.1 percent, reflecting the removal of a large rise in the March 1996 quarter.
-- Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
